name: Gros Morne National Park
story: Gros Morne National Park covers 1,805 km2 on the west coast of Newfoundland, Canada. Named after Newfoundland's second-highest mountain peak, it features coastal, forest, bog, and alpine habitats. The park protects eroded remnants of a mountain range formed 1.2 billion years ago and showcases the process of continental drift.
matters: The park was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987 for its geological history and exceptional scenery, illustrating the concept of plate tectonics. It also supports a wide range of terrestrial and marine wildlife across its habitats.
